claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or equivalent support) towards his care - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out - I give about £10 a week towards his things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess whether your contributions are sufficient, I need to know a bit more:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, the person he lives with)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask you this:

**Who does Alex live with currently, and what is your relationship to Alex (are you his parent, legal guardian, or another relation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his other parent - my ex-partner. I'm his parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Now, to properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand more about your contribution. You mentioned you give about £10 a week towards Alex's things.

**Can you tell me what the current weekly Child Benefit rate is, or do you know if your £10 per week contribution is at least equal to what Child Benefit would pay for one child?**

For context, to qualify for Child Benefit when you don't live with your child, you need to be contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit pays (or equivalent support in kind) towards looking after them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't know what the Child Benefit rate is, to be honest. I just give the £10 a week to help with his clothes and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. Let me help clarify the situation for you.

Based on the rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. To be eligible when you don't live with your child, you need to be paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money.

Since you're not sure of the current Child Benefit rate, and you don't know if anyone else (like your ex-partner who Alex lives with) is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, I have a couple more questions:

**Are you making these £10 weekly payments under a court order or formal maintenance agreement, or are these informal voluntary contributions?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: These are just informal contributions - there's no court order or formal agreement. I just help out when I can with what he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Would you be able to find out from your ex-partner whether they are currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child, and typically the person the child lives with would be the one claiming. If your ex-partner is already claiming, you wouldn't be eligible to claim for Alex as well.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I can try to find out, but we don't really communicate that well. Is there any other way to check, or can you tell me what happens if they are claiming?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that communication can be difficult. Unfortunately, I don't have a way to check for you whether your ex-partner is claiming - you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office directly to inquire about that.

However, let me explain the situation based on what you've told me:

**The key points are:**
- Only one person can get Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex lives with your ex-partner (his other parent)
- You contribute £10 per week informally towards his care
- You don't know the current Child Benefit rate or if your contributions meet or exceed that amount
- You're uncertain whether your ex-partner is already claiming

Given this situation, let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**If you were to find out that your ex-partner is NOT claiming Child Benefit for Alex, would you be able and willing to increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate (if £10 per week is less than that rate)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I mean, I'm not sure I could afford more than what I'm giving now. The £10 a week is what I can manage at the moment. But are you saying that if my ex isn't claiming, I might be able to get it? What exactly is the rate anyway?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
